description:
## Goal

Invert ownership so that `OctoPi.Coder.Loop` is the orchestrator that drives `OctoPi.Agent`'s transcript and compaction lifecycle, and the Agent kernel becomes passive about both — its `loop.messages` is just "the chain Coder asked me to run on," and it has zero knowledge of compaction, thresholds, branch summaries, or session navigation.

This mirrors upstream pi-mono's split: `packages/agent` knows nothing about compaction (zero references in `agent.ts` / `agent-loop.ts` / `types.ts`); `packages/coding-agent`'s `AgentSession` orchestrates everything by calling `agent.abort()`, doing the work, and writing `agent.state.messages = sessionContext.messages` directly.

## Why

The current architecture carries vestiges from when `OctoPi.Agent` was meant to be runnable standalone:

- `messages_provider` exists as a per-turn override of Agent's read path because we never trusted Agent's `MessageLog` to stay in sync with Coder's `:path`.
- `MessageLog` is a parallel transcript Agent maintains independently — kept current via streamed pushes, but bypassed for the LLM read.
- `CompactionRequested` / `compaction_response` is an event round-trip baked into the kernel that exists because Coder couldn't directly mutate Agent's state.
- `pending_compact_from` (added in opi-qy9) is the defer-reply scaffolding that compensates for the round-trip.
- `Coder.Loop.State.path` is the third copy of the linearization (tree → path → MessageLog).

Upstream avoids all of this. The Agent kernel has one transcript (`state.messages`), the host writes into it directly, and the host owns when to compact. The kernel is dumb on purpose.

## Scope (in)

- Replace `messages_provider` with a stateless `convert_to_llm` callback (required at start_link).
- Add `Agent.push_message/2` and `Agent.set_messages/2` host-write APIs.
- Widen Agent's message type to `AgentMessage = AI.Message | CompactionSummaryMessage | BranchSummaryMessage | …` so synthetic types live inside the buffer; `convert_to_llm` is the boundary that flattens them.
- Move all compaction triggering out of Agent.Loop (manual, auto-post-turn, auto-pre-prompt) into Coder.Loop.
- Delete `CompactionRequested`, `compaction_response`, `Agent.compact`, the auto-compact threshold logic, `pending_compact_from`, the spawn-and-callback plumbing.
- Branch summary / navigation: same pattern as compaction (Coder runs work, calls `Agent.set_messages`).
- Drop `Coder.Loop.State.path`. Compaction prep reads `SessionStore.path/3` on demand.
- Inline `MessageLog` to a plain list of `AgentMessage`.

## Scope (out)

- JSONL on-disk format. Byte-identical before and after.
- Entry types and tree structure in `SessionStore`.
- Extension event surface (`:session_before_compact`, `:session_compact`, `:session_tree`, etc.) — same events fire, just from Coder instead of round-tripped through Agent.
- Upstream parity. **This is purely a control-flow inversion.**

## Constraint

This is a port. Compaction outcomes (summary contents, kept-tail boundary, persistence semantics) and the JSONL format are byte-identical to upstream pi-mono before and after this epic. Verify by replaying upstream-generated session files: round-trip → compact → round-trip stays byte-stable.

## Done when

- `OctoPi.Agent.Loop` has zero references to compaction, thresholds, or branch summaries.
- `MessageLog` module is gone; `Agent.Loop.State.messages` is `[AgentMessage]`.
- `Coder.Loop.State.path` is gone; compaction prep pulls linearization from `SessionStore` on demand.
- `messages_provider` is gone; `convert_to_llm` is the only Coder→Agent transform hook.
- All existing tests green; round-trip JSONL parity preserved with a test session file generated by upstream pi-mono.
title: Coder owns the orchestrator; Agent kernel goes passive on transcript and compaction
